newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries edge higher, market quiet ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries edge higher, market quiet ahead of CPI.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries in London were better bid on Tuesday but there was little activity as the market awaited U.S. March consumer price data, traders said.

"Prices are a couple of ticks higher across the curve but every one is waiting for the CPI and nothing much is likely to happen before that," said Nick Benton, U.S. Treasuries trader at BankAmerica in London.
He said the market was exceptionally quiet and trading was very thin.
The long bond was at 93-12 to yield 7.17 percent by 0935 GMT, compared with 93-07 in Tokyo and 93-10 in New York.
Two-year T-bonds were at 99-16, yielding 6.52 percent, unchanged from 99-16 at both the Tokyo and New York closes.
The 10-year benchmark T-bond was at 94.31, to yield 6.96 percent compared with 94-28 in Tokyo and New York.

U.S. March consumer prices are due at 1230 GMT. A Reuters poll of economists is forecasting a rise of 0.2 percent versus a 0.3 percent rise in February. Core CPI (excluding food and energy) is forecast to rise 0.3 percent, compared with a 0.2 percent rise previously.

Analysts said the market would be looking for further signs of inflationary pressures, with many players expecting the Federal Reserve to raise rates again at the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

Jim Fralick, senior economist at Morgan Stanley in London, said last Friday's sell off coupled with the strength implied by the retail sales numbers meant market attention had now rotated back to the price data.
He said some of the rise in the consumer prices would be due to the impositon of an excise tax on air fares.
"Given the special nature of that, the market will probably try to strip it out and we will see further consolidation going forwards," Fralick said.
Other economic data to be released on Tuesday includes February business inventories at 1230 GMT and March real earnings at 1400 GMT.
June T-bond futures were at 106-26, up 4/32 in automated trade.
